item.title: Trump tells Zelenskyy to stop doing 'one thing' during attacks on Russia
item.description: President Donald Trump told reporters he wants Volodymyr Zelensky to stop hitting Russian diesel refineries, saying the strikes are causing a global fuel shortage.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump has a blunt message for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as Kyiv continues targeting Russia: Stop hitting its diesel refineries.

Trump made the remarks Sunday while attending the Irish Open at his golf club in Doonbeg, Ireland, after a reporter asked whether he had spoken with Zelenskyy following a recent conversation with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"Zelensky has to do one thing. He has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia," Trump told reporters.

TRUMP NEGOTIATORS WITKOFF, KUSHNER MEET WITH PUTIN IN MOSCOW AS US PUSHES FOR END TO RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR

Trump said Ukraine could continue pursuing other targets inside Russia but urged Zelenskyy to steer clear of the country’s diesel infrastructure.

"Let him go after targets, but not diesel fuel because he's causing a shortage of diesel," Trump said. "This isn't done by the Middle East. This is done by what's happening with Russia and Ukraine."

The president said he had already spoken directly with Zelenskyy about the issue.

"So we spoke to Mr. Zelensky about it. There are plenty of other targets," Trump said. "Don't hit diesel fuel because that's hurting the world. We don't want him to hit diesel fuel. He's hitting diesel refineries."

WATCH: FIGHTS BREAK OUT AT RUSSIAN GAS STATIONS AS PUTIN ADMITS FUEL SHORTAGES

Trump’s remarks come as Ukraine has targeted Russia’s oil and gas infrastructure with long-range strikes, part of Kyiv’s effort to hamper an industry that provides revenue and fuel for Moscow’s war effort. Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.

The strikes have put pressure on Russia’s fuel supplies, prompting rationing in parts of the country and a Russian ban on diesel exports in July. The disruption has also added pressure to global diesel supplies, which have faced additional strain amid reduced oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

Diesel prices in the U.S. climbed above an average of $6 per gallon on Friday, reaching a record high.

Russia has intensified its aerial attacks on Ukraine in recent weeks, including strikes involving ballistic missiles and drones, while Ukraine has continued targeting sites inside Russia.

Russian and Ukrainian officials reported another round of large-scale drone attacks overnight into Sunday, with casualties reported on both sides.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump team unloads on liberal journalist over Natalie Harp posts: ‘Sick, deluded freak’
item.description: The White House fired back at Aaron Rupar over his #TravelWithNatalie posts about aide Natalie Harp joining Trump on his Ireland trip.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration blasted liberal journalist Aaron Rupar on Saturday after he highlighted White House executive assistant Natalie Harp accompanying President Donald Trump on his trip to Ireland, extending weeks of scrutiny surrounding the 35-year-old aide that began after Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff invoked her name during a campaign speech.

The White House-run Rapid Response 47 account responded directly after Rupar posted a photo of Harp during the president's trip and captioned it, "Look who made the trip to Ireland!" with his recurring #TravelWithNatalie hashtag.

"President Trump does, in fact, travel with staff. Aaron, on the other hand, is a sick, deluded freak (in his 40s) who sits behind a keyboard and posts creepy things like this," the account shared.

CNN, MS NOW HAVE MENTIONED TRUMP AIDE NATALIE HARP HUNDREDS OF TIMES SINCE OSSOFF'S VIRAL JAB

Rupar has repeatedly highlighted Harp's appearances alongside Trump in recent weeks and used #TravelWithNatalie, including posts about her traveling with the president and one referring to what he called Trump's "gigantic diaper bag." His focus followed Osoff's remark last month that propelled the White House staffer into extensive cable-news coverage.

"The taxpayer-funded White House incitement account is now attacking me for [checks notes] being in my 40s", shared on X in response to the Rapid Response 47 post.

NewsBusters Executive Editor Tim Graham told Fox News Digital on Sunday that Rupar’s continued use of the travel reference was deliberately playing off the controversy generated by Ossoff’s original remark.

"Rupar knows he is trolling for the Trump haters. The whole 'travels with Natalie' line is toying with the original Ossoff affair smear," Graham said.

OBAMA STRATEGIST TURNS ON RISING DEM STAR OVER VIRAL TRUMP ATTACK: 'GRATUITOUS AND UNNECESSARY'

The attention surrounding Harp began after Sen. Ossoff, D-Ga., invoked her by first name while criticizing Trump during a campaign speech. Conservatives interpreted Ossoff's remarks as insinuating an inappropriate relationship between Trump and Harp, an interpretation Ossoff later rejected.

Ossoff made the reference while accusing Trump of being more interested in personal pursuits than carrying out presidential duties.

"He doesn’t want to do the job. He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the emir of Qatar," Ossoff said.

HOUSE DEM'S 'LAKE NATALIE' JAB AT TRUMP AIDE SETS SOCIAL MEDIA ABLAZE: 'STAY CLASSY'

Fox News Digital reached out to Rupar, the White House and Ossoff for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

Ossoff later faced questions from MS Now host Jen Psaki about why he specifically named Harp. He denied suggesting an affair and instead said his reference was about the advisors surrounding Trump.

"Well, I've heard this particular aide referred to as his security blanket, and I think we could say that about any number of the senior aides in the White House," Ossoff said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The White House responded forcefully to Ossoff’s initial remarks, defending Harp as one of Trump’s top aides.

"Natalie Harp is one of the most loyal and hardest working aides on President Trump's team. Jon Ossoff is a cringeworthy, feminine theatre kid cosplaying as Barack Obama. Nobody gives a s--- what this lightweight loser says," White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

In August, Fox News Digital reported that CNN and MS NOW had mentioned Harp hundreds of times in the days following Ossoff's remarks, after CNN alone had mentioned her at least 132 times by Aug. 19.

Graham previously told Fox News Digital that the coverage surrounding Harp was failing to address what he considered the "fundamental question" about why her routine presence alongside the president had become a major media story.

item.title: Popular GLP-1 weight-loss drugs linked to potentially deadly brain disorder
item.description: A study linked 15 cases of Wernicke encephalopathy to GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic and Mounjaro, raising concerns about vitamin B1 deficiency risks.
item.content:encoded:
Researchers are warning about a rare but potentially life-threatening brain condition that may be linked to popular GLP-1 weight-loss medications.

A new study, published in Clinical Nutrition, identified 15 reported cases of Wernicke encephalopathy, a neurological disorder caused by severe vitamin B1 deficiency, in people taking GLP-1 receptor agonists.

Most of the reported cases involved semaglutide, sold under the brand names Ozempic and Wegovy, or tirzepatide, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound.

DOCTORS REVEAL HIDDEN DANGER FOR SOME OZEMPIC, WEGOVY USERS WITH BRAIN DISORDERS

Researchers found 15 cases through the FDA's Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), published medical literature and their own medical center.

Most patients reported gastrointestinal symptoms or nutritional issues, including weight loss, vomiting, loss of appetite or malnutrition, the study noted.

Reports of the disorder appeared more often among people taking GLP-1 medications than among those taking other drugs, the researchers found. They emphasized, however, that the study cannot prove the medications caused the condition.

Vitamin B1 plays an important role in brain function, the researchers said. Severe deficiencies can cause confusion, trouble walking, balance problems and vision changes. If left untreated, the condition can lead to permanent neurological damage or death.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Karthik Achari, a Chicago-based clinician and founder of PepMD who was not involved in the study, said the findings should be viewed in perspective.

"Researchers went through adverse event reports and the medical literature and found a small number of cases, 15, of Wernicke encephalopathy in people taking GLP-1 drugs," Achari told Fox News Digital. "That's out of millions of people on these medications. So this is rare."

"But it's real, it's serious, and the mechanism makes sense," he added.

GLP-1 medications can reduce appetite while also causing nausea and vomiting, making it easier for some people to become deficient in vitamin B1, Achari said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"The drug shrinks your appetite. It doesn't shrink your body's requirements," he said. "You can now eat very little without feeling it, which is the point of the medication, but your need for protein, vitamins, and fluids didn't go anywhere."

People with persistent nausea and vomiting, those losing weight very quickly while eating little, people with a history of bariatric surgery and those who use alcohol heavily may face a higher risk, Achari said.

Erin Palinski-Wade, a New Jersey-based nutritionist and author of "The Sleepdemic Solution," said proper nutrition and hydration should be considered part of treatment while taking GLP-1 medications.

"GLP-1 medications can dramatically reduce appetite, but that also means people may unintentionally under-eat the very things their bodies need most, especially protein, fiber and fluids," she told Fox News Digital.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Palinski-Wade said ongoing vomiting or diarrhea can increase the risk of dehydration and kidney problems. She urged patients to seek medical guidance if those symptoms continue for roughly 24 hours.

"Don't assume every side effect is just part of being on a GLP-1," Palinski-Wade said. "Severe or persistent symptoms deserve attention."

The researchers acknowledged that the study relied largely on reports submitted to the FDA and cannot prove GLP-1 medications caused the condition. They called for additional research, and experts said patients should not stop taking prescribed GLP-1 medications based on these findings alone.

Fox News Digital reached out to Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly and the researchers for comment.

item.title: Cruise passengers erupt over 'rude' luggage habit that sharply divides travelers
item.description: Etiquette expert Diane Gottsman of Texas weighed in on the heated cruise elevator debate about travelers using rolling suitcases on packed disembarkation day mornings.
item.content:encoded:
Cruise passengers are debating a heated topic among vacation travelers who take to the ocean.

Does bringing luggage into crowded ship elevators cross a major etiquette line, especially on hectic disembarkation mornings?

Those carrying their own bags often depend on elevators to move between decks as thousands of passengers prepare to leave the ship. Now, social media posts are fueling a broader argument over whether squeezing suitcases into packed elevators is practical or just plain rude.

OUTRAGED CRUISE PASSENGERS SOUND OFF ABOUT ‘IMMENSE DISAPPOINTMENT’ AFTER ABRUPT CANCELLATION

Diane Gottsman, an etiquette expert based in Texas, said passengers can bring luggage into elevators, though they should be considerate of the limited space.

"When it comes to traveling, space is a priority," Gottsman told Fox News Digital. "You always have to think about the people that are going to be around you."

Gottsman said passengers can leave larger suitcases outside their cabin the night before for crew members to collect.

"When possible, it's always best to keep your suitcases to a minimum when getting on a crowded cruise ship elevator," she said.

MAJOR AIRLINE ROASTS PASSENGERS WHO JUMP UP RIGHT AFTER LANDING, IGNITING FIERCE BACKLASH

Passengers who prefer to carry their own luggage can do so, she added, but should be prepared to manage it themselves.

Cruise lines also have their own procedures for handling bags.

Carnival Cruise Line states on its website that checked baggage service during embarkation ends two hours before a ship's scheduled sailing time.

"Guests arriving after this time will be responsible for taking their bags on board," the cruise line states.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Planning ahead is especially important on busy embarkation and disembarkation days, Gottsman said.

"We know when we're getting off a cruise ship, it's going to be busy," she said. "Everyone is getting off the same cruise ship. So you have to plan in advance."

She advised passengers to let others exit before boarding and wait for another elevator if one is already packed.

"Don't just charge on with your luggage," Gottsman said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Passengers with mobility issues should also be given priority, while those with extra luggage should be prepared to wait, she added.

The issue recently surfaced on Reddit after a first-time cruiser said the traveler and partner were scoffed at by another passenger while taking an elevator from Deck 14 to Deck 5 with their rolling suitcases.

Many cruisers defended the couple — arguing that elevators are often the most practical option for passengers carrying luggage across multiple decks.

"I always hand-roll my luggage off. I always use the elevator," one Reddit user wrote. "I'm not hauling my bags up and down stairs."

Another commenter asked, "How else would you get your luggage down that many decks?"

Said another person, "People find any reason to complain [about] a ship elevator. My mom was on a scooter [due to] her bad back/knees, and people were so rude to her at the elevators."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Yet another person chimed in, "The rudeness always seems higher on disembarkation day. You didn’t do anything wrong. I would only use the stairs if it was a flight or two just to save time, otherwise I would definitely use it."

Other cruisers said bringing luggage into an elevator is fine as long as passengers remain considerate of those around them.

"You can absolutely use the elevators, just be cognizant of others and make space when you can," one commenter wrote.

Some disagreed, arguing that using the ship's luggage service can make departure easier for everyone.

"The whole point of the luggage delivery is to make it easier for everyone," one person wrote.

Cruise industry experts projected a worldwide increase in the number of people taking to the ocean this year — breaking last year’s record, The Associated Press reported several months ago. 

In an April report released by the Cruise Lines International Association, an estimated 38.3 million people were projected to travel on ships this year — a number that's 4% higher than last year’s 37.2 million record-breaking number of passengers.

item.title: Election chaos in this red state just got even stranger for Republicans after Supreme Court ruling
item.description: The Supreme Court blocked Missouri's new congressional map, forcing the state to use 2022 boundaries that favor Emanuel Cleaver's Kansas City district.
item.content:encoded:
Republicans suffered a fresh blow in Missouri after the Supreme Court blocked a congressional map that could have helped the GOP gain another House seat in November.

The ruling, handed down last week, means Missouri will use its 2022 congressional map instead of the new boundaries backed by President Donald Trump and Missouri Republicans.

Missouri held its August primary under the new map, meaning candidates won their party nominations based on one set of district boundaries. But those boundaries will change before the November election, when Missouri is expected to return to its 2022 map.

TRUMP DANGLES $5,000 CHECKS AS DEBT SURGES — BUT ONLY IF GOP CAN CLEAR MAJOR MIDTERM HURDLE

Typically, states redraw their congressional and state legislative districts once every decade after the Census to account for population changes and ensure that each district has roughly the same number of residents.

The new map would have shifted parts of Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver’s Kansas City district into more Republican-leaning areas, making the seat more competitive.

Republicans hoped the changes would help them win seven of Missouri’s eight House seats in the November midterm elections. The GOP currently holds six of the state’s eight seats, while Democrats hold two.

Missouri must now use the 2022 map, which keeps Cleaver’s district more favorable to Democrats.

The Supreme Court’s decision came after more than a year of legal battles over which congressional map Missouri should use.

Missouri held its August primary under the new map, but the state will use its 2022 district boundaries for the November general election. That means some voters could be assigned to a different congressional district in November than the one in which they voted during the primary.

The change could affect more than 1 million voters, or nearly one-fourth of Missouri’s electorate, according to an Associated Press estimate.

The conflicting court orders have added to the confusion, with the November election just weeks away. Candidates and election officials must now adjust to the 2022 boundaries.

MISSOURI HIGH COURT BLOCKS GOP-BACKED CONGRESSIONAL MAPS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS; TRUMP BLASTS 'RIDICULOUS' RULING

The Supreme Court did not explain its reasoning in the brief order.

The White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

item.title: FIBA Secretary General Andreas Zagklis speaks out on Caitlin Clark's impact on growth of World Cup
item.description: FIBA's secretary general says Caitlin Clark and women's basketball stars could surpass male players in popularity at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
item.content:encoded:
FIBA Secretary General Andreas Zagklis addressed the impact of Caitlin Clark and other new young players playing in the World Cup for the first time on the tournament's growth and visibility.

Zagklis, speaking at a press conference before the World Cup Final against France, called Clark one of the biggest stars of her generation and predicted that the popularity of the women's basketball players could surpass the men's at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

"I think what these players, Caitlin, one of them, have done in increasing the popularity of the women's game is incredible. We should feel very proud about them. And I can tell you, me and my team have been supportive of what USA Basketball and each and every national member federation coming into the World Cup had planned for their promotion. And we tried to amplify that experience. They themselves, the players said this is a unique moment for them," Zagklis said.

THE PREDOMINANT BASKETBALL DYNASTY ON EARTH IS AT STAKE AS AMERICA'S EYES TURN TO CAITLIN CLARK'S ROLE

"So while I may not be able to quantify the answer and give you exact numbers, but our team perhaps can do that after the tournament, I can tell you that the popularity of our women's game, of Caitlin as one of the biggest stars, not the biggest star of this generation has done. We see this with Iyana Martin from Spain, MVP of the under-19 in 2023. And she signed a big sponsorship agreement herself just with a FIBA partner two days before the tournament.

"So players around the world are picking up these opportunities. And I'm extremely proud of them. And I can tell you, I do believe that in the Los Angeles Olympics, our female players may be at the same or even higher level of popularity than many of our former male players. And this is not a criticism to anybody. It's just a result of the collective growth of the game. And we're proud for both the male and female players that we have to admit have made our sport as global as it is today."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Clark has become one the biggest storylines of this year's tournament, and has done so without even starting a game.

Clark has come off the bench in each of Team USA's five wins, alongside fellow young stars Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers, as coach Kara Lawson has opted to play the veteran starters in all five of the U.S. wins.

Still, Clark has been among the tournament's top performers.

The 24-year-old guard has clocked just over 20 minutes per game, placing her among the team's most utilized players. In those minutes, she has proven to be an elite facilitator, currently ranking third in the entire World Cup with 5.8 assists per game.

Her playmaking was most obvious in the team's opening victory over China, where she immediately accelerated the American offense to the tune of 14 points and a record-setting 11 assists without committing a single turnover.

item.title: Viral video shows bystanders warning elderly man who has no clue he's being followed by a huge black bear
item.description: Video with over 35 million views captures a black bear silently following an elderly man down a British Columbia sidewalk before bystanders intervene.
item.content:encoded:
An elderly man had what has been labeled a "close call" with a black bear, although he wasn’t initially aware of the fact that a bear was following him as he shuffled down the sidewalk. Not until it was pointed out to him.

The video of the man, the bear, and the bystanders pointing out that he's being followed was posted on Instagram by Quail guy. It has more than 35 million views and when you see how close the bear is to the man you understand why.

The man, reportedly in British Columbia, is shuffling along on a sidewalk holding a bag minding his own business. He walks by a black bear seemingly not even noticing that it's just feet from him.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

Bystanders across the street try to warn him that the rather large bear is behind him and appears to be following him. After he realizes what they're saying, the man turns and looks at the bear, then picks up the pace as he continues walking.

And by picking up the pace, I mean he goes from almost standing still to actually standing still before taking off, probably as fast as he can shuffle his feet.

6 OF THE BEST FALL CAMPING DESTINATIONS IN AMERICA, PLUS GEAR BEGINNERS SHOULD PACK

The concerned group of bystanders did what they set out to do. They warned the man. They were loud enough to get the bear to turn around, and they didn’t step foot off of the sidewalk from across the street.

Another potential disaster avoided. The old man presumably made it the rest of the way home without unknowingly wandering into another close call with nature or anything else.

PIZZA DELIVERY MAN DESERVES A RAISE AFTER WALKING PAST A BLACK BEAR TO DELIVER CUSTOMER'S ORDER

Just as important was someone documenting it all on video. You hope for the best in that type of situation, but if it does go sideways, you have some game film to study and learn from.

item.title: Obama privately sounds alarm on ‘dangerous’ AI, urges Democrats to put issue at center of agenda
item.description: Barack Obama warned AI could become dangerous without greater oversight and urged Hakeem Jeffries to launch a very public conversation on it.
item.content:encoded:
Former President Barack Obama urged Democrats during a private fundraiser in New York City on Thursday to place artificial intelligence near the center of their political agenda ahead of the midterms and 2028 presidential race while warning that the technology could become dangerous without greater oversight as voters increasingly raise concerns about jobs, privacy and data centers.

Obama, speaking alongside House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., warned party donors and lawmakers that policymakers risk losing control of an industry developing largely in private hands, The New York Times reported.

"This is something that is moving very fast in private hands, and if we don’t get on top of it, I think can be dangerous," Obama said. "If we do get on top of it, I do think it’s beneficial. I genuinely think it’s going to accelerate, for example, drug development in ways that can help us cure diseases. I do think that this can help us figure out pathways for a clean energy future."

RNC member and Humans First Chairwoman Amy Kremer told Fox News Digital on Sunday that she agreed policymakers need to recognize both AI’s benefits and risks, but pushed back on turning greater authority over to the federal government or technology companies.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

"You don't have to agree on politics to recognize reality: AI is moving incredibly fast, and policymakers need to understand both the opportunities and the very real risks that come with it," Kremer told Fox News Digital. "Where I likely disagree with President Obama is on what government should do about it. The answer isn't handing Washington bureaucrats more control, and it certainly isn't allowing Big Tech to write the rules that govern itself."

"We need guardrails that protect Americans while allowing American innovation to lead the world. That means protecting children, workers and our national security, while making sure China doesn't win the AI race," she continued.

Obama's warning comes as Fox News Digital polling found substantial voter resistance to the infrastructure powering the AI boom.

A July Fox News poll found 70% of registered voters opposed construction of AI data centers in their communities, compared with 30% who supported them.

MAGA BEGINS TO CRACK AS 2026 GOP ROSTER BACKS AWAY FROM TRUMP'S TECH VISION

The debate has also divided Republicans as data centers become a more prominent midterm issue. Several Republican candidates have called for limits or pauses on new projects despite President Donald Trump's support for expanding data-center development.

At the closed-door fundraiser, Obama directly urged Jeffries to prepare Democrats to make AI policy a public issue if the party takes control of the House.

"Once you are speaker, I would strongly urge that the Democrats put together a framework for a very public conversation," Obama said.

Obama also urged prospective 2028 presidential candidates to develop a "very clear plan" for AI and make the technology one of their "central agendas," according to the partial transcript provided by his office to The New York Times. He identified potential job displacement and effects on children among the issues candidates should address.

Public anxiety extends beyond data centers. An April Fox News poll found 63% of voters believed AI hurts privacy, while 56% said it hurts U.S. job creation. Just 21% said the technology helps job creation.

DEMOCRATS SOUND ALARM OVER AI JOB APOCALYPSE — BUT LABOR MARKET ISN'T FOLLOWING SCRIPT

Trump has emphasized rapid AI development and maintaining the United States' competitive position against China. His administration unveiled its first national AI policy framework in March, calling for a consistent national standard while addressing issues including free speech, child safety and energy costs.

"The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor," Trump said.

Concerns about AI accelerated again Saturday when Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing the development race, warning that advances could outpace humans' ability to understand and control the systems. Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman subsequently expressed support for Amodei's call.

Jeffries backed Obama’s call for action and sought to draw a contrast with Republicans.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"President Obama is correct that decisive action must be taken on artificial intelligence," Jeffries said, adding that "Republicans have abdicated their responsibility to govern on behalf of the American people. We will not repeat their error."

House Democrats are already developing an AI policy framework that is expected to be released this fall after review by Jeffries, according to The New York Times.

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House and Palantir for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Female passenger undresses on American Airlines flight, engages in 'indecent acts,' crew reports
item.description: A female passenger on American Airlines Flight 1779 reportedly undressed and performed indecent acts mid-flight, prompting law enforcement at Miami.
item.content:encoded:
Law enforcement officers met an American Airlines flight upon its arrival at Miami International Airport late Friday night following reports of a female passenger undressing and behaving indecently mid-flight.

American Airlines Flight 1779 departed Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport (BWI) just after 9 p.m. EDT on Friday, Sept. 11, 2025, nearly two hours behind its scheduled departure time, according to public flight-tracking data. The flight landed in Miami at approximately 11:23 p.m. EDT.

As the Airbus A319 was en route to Florida, flight attendants alerted the cockpit crew to a disturbance involving a passenger in row 9.

UNRULY PASSENGERS COULD BE BANNED FOR LIFE FROM MULTIPLE AIRLINES UNDER NEW PROPOSAL

According to Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS) datalink logs published by aviation website AirLive, the lead flight attendant reported that a female passenger in seat 9D had completely undressed and engaged in indecent acts in view of nearby passengers.

The ACARS message stated the incident was required to be reported to American Airlines’ Integrated Operations Center and that law enforcement should be requested.

FRONTIER PASSENGERS TACKLE MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY CHOKED OFF-DUTY FLIGHT ATTENDANT, TRIED TO OPEN DOOR MID-FLIGHT

The flight continued to Miami without diverting and arrived at Gate D2 in Terminal N, according to flight tracking service Flightera. AirLive reported that law enforcement officers were waiting at the gate and that the passenger was taken into custody.

It remains unclear what specific measures cabin crew took during the flight to manage the disturbance.

Fox News Digital has reached out to American Airlines, the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office and Miami International Airport for comment.

item.title: Hits keep coming as Rams lose Myles Garrett for at least four games after looming knee surgery
item.description: Myles Garrett will undergo knee surgery and land on injured reserve, costing the Los Angeles Rams their prized acquisition for at least four games.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams had a great offseason but the start of the regular season has been a disaster and Myles Garrett needing knee surgery is perhaps the worst part of that.

The Rams will be placing their signature offseason acquisition and 2025 Defensive Player of the Year on injured reserve, a source confirmed to OutKick.

That means Garrett, who missed considerable practice time during training camp because of a troublesome knee situation, will miss a minimum of four games.

'WE BACK': AARON DONALD RETURNS TO THE RAMS AND A DEFENSE NOW LOADED WITH MYLES GARRETT AND OTHERS

Garrett will miss games against the New York Giants, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles, and Buffalo Bills.

He could actually miss more games, depending on his recovery and the success of the upcoming surgery.

The good news is the surgery is scheduled as an arthroscopy initially meant to perform a trim rather than a full-blown repair. If that initial expectation based on MRI scans holds, the four-week timetable should be an accurate expectation.

RAMS' DISASTER IN AUSTRALIA RAISES THE QUESTION: SHOULD THE TEAM HAVE FOLLOWED THE 49ERS THERE EARLIER?

The Rams, the Super Bowl favorite among many pundits before the season began, lost their Week 1 game against the San Francisco 49ers.

They did not have Aaron Donald for that game as his ramp-up period after returning from a two-year retirement was not considered complete and the team wanted to be cautious.

That caution will remain but the Rams obviously need Donald sooner than later now that they will be without Garrett for a while.

item.title: Tim Scott fires back after ‘Morning Joe’ mocks fiery GOP speech, accuses program of hiding 'from the truth'
item.description: Tim Scott fired back at Joe Scarborough and the "Morning Joe" panel after they mocked his fiery speech at the Republican midterm convention.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., fired back at a "Morning Joe" panel during an appearance on "Saturday in America" after the MS NOW hosts mocked his fiery speech at the Republican midterm convention and jokingly prayed for him on air.

Scott dismissed the criticism and accused the program of hiding "from the truth," doubling down on his assertion that Democrats "hate what it means to be American."

"At the end of the day, now we know why Joe's ratings are so darn low. They will hide from the truth, and they will publicly endorse a lie," he said.

"I know they're coming for our culture. This is a group of Democrats, the most dangerous, radical and weird group of Democrats, who literally say there are six genders and God is non-binary. If you don't want to stand up and fight for the soul of this country, your wood is wet. It's that simple."

Scott made his impassioned speech at the Republican Party's first-ever midterm convention. The GOP convened in Dallas to rally voters as it fights to keep control of Congress in November.

During the convention, Scott declared, "The only way to keep dangerous, radical, weird out of the Senate is a united Republican Party, standing with our President, Donald J. Trump! Stand for the president, Donald J. Trump!"

JOE SCARBOROUGH GOES SCORCHED EARTH ON DEMOCRATS NOT SEPARATING THEMSELVES FROM HASAN PIKER

"This is a battle for the heart of our nation. I said, the heart of our nation! The Democrats’ extreme candidates won’t rip that heart out of our chests!" Scott said.

"They hate our culture," he added. "They hate what it means to be American. Hear me, Dallas. Not! On! Our! Watch! We will not back down. We will not grow weary."

"Morning Joe" co-host Joe Scarborough called Scott's speech "really weird," adding, "I thought for a moment there, he needs some anti-seizure medication."

CAN THE 'BEST SHOWMAN IN POLITICS' DELIVER AGAIN? GOP BETS ON TRUMP AT HISTORIC MIDTERM CONVENTION

The panel, including Al Sharpton, joined hands shortly thereafter and jokingly prayed for him.

item.title: 'Team Mom' Alison Lee completes largest comeback in Solheim Cup history for Team USA to cap off unbeaten week
item.description: Alison Lee erased a record 4-down deficit in her Solheim Cup singles match against Esther Henseleit, rewriting 36 years of competition history.
item.content:encoded:
Alison Lee began the 2026 LPGA Tour season in the broadcast booth while on maternity leave after giving birth to her son in April of last year. The 31-year-old earning a spot on the U.S. Solheim Cup team was remarkable in and of itself, but what she accomplished for the red, white, and blue against the Europeans in the Netherlands was stunning.

Lee teed it up in three of the first four sessions at the biennial event, and cruised to victories in her two foursome matches and one fourball match across the opening two days. She was the second American to tee off to begin Sunday's singles session, and while it quickly seemed she had run out of steam, she reminded the world that things are not always as they appear.

Lee played her first 11 holes at 1-over par and stepped onto the 12th tee 4-down in her match against Europe's Esther Henseleit at Bernardus Golf. No player in the 36-year history of the competition had erased a deficit of that size in a singles match, yet somehow, some way, the "Team Mom" found a different gear and rewrote the history books.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Henseleit playing the final seven holes of Sunday's match at 2-over helped Lee's comeback effort, but the American still had to get the ball in the hole, and that she did.

Lee played the final seven holes at 4-under, and did not just go on to tie the match and secure a half point for the U.S., but she earned a full point with birdies on two of her final three holes.

Lee became the first player to automatically qualify for the U.S. Solheim Cup team after giving birth since Hall of Famer Juli Inkster did the same in 2011.

The former UCLA star did not make her first start on the LPGA Tour until mid-April, upon her return from maternity leave, leaving her a very tight window of opportunity to accumulate points and even get on the radar of U.S. captain Angela Stanford.

Across her 12 starts on the LPGA Tour leading up to the Solheim Cup, Lee earned three top-10 finishes, including a T-5 finish at the KPMG Women's PGA Championship in June.

Lee's early victory on Sunday was one of only a few bright spots for the Americans on the final day as Team Europe ultimately secured the victory thanks to England's Lottie Woad defeating Auston Kim 2&1 in the eighth match of the afternoon.

Lee was in the early stages of her pregnancy at the 2024 Solheim Cup, with only U.S. captain Stacy Lewis, her four-ball partner Megan Khang, and her caddie being aware of the major life news at the start of the competition. She earned one point for the Americans to help secure a 15.5-12.5 victory.

Prior to Lee teeing it up in 2026, Suzann Pettersen, a captain’s pick for Team Europe in 2019, was the last mom to play for either side in the event. She won the cup for the Europeans in dramatic fashion and immediately retired.

item.title: Jesus' crucifixion account gets fresh look after ancient ring tied to Pilate is reinterpreted
item.description: Offering new clues about Jesus' crucifixion, an ancient ring found at Herodium may reveal how Pontius Pilate delegated authority in Roman Judea. Experts shared insights.
item.content:encoded:
New research about an ancient ring bearing an inscription linked to Pontius Pilate may reveal fresh clues about how the Roman governor wielded authority — nearly 2,000 years after he sentenced Jesus Christ to death.

The ring, discovered at Herodium, a mountaintop fortress in the Judean desert, in the 1960s, has long been known to archaeologists — but a new interpretation could help explain its connection to Pilate.

The 2,000-year-old ring sat in storage for over 50 years before researchers published details about it in 2018, according to a release from the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA).

AUTHOR DINESH D'SOUZA CHALLENGES BIBLE SKEPTICS WITH 'STARTLING' ARCHAEOLOGICAL DISCOVERIES

A later study challenged its connection to Pilate altogether, setting up the scholarly debate that Catherine Bonesho, a UCLA professor of ancient Judaism, addressed in a new study published in Palestine Exploration Quarterly.

Bonesho concluded that the ring's wording was a transliteration of the Latin PILATO — meaning "for Pilate" or "to Pilate" — into Greek letters.

This theory, Bonesho argued, better explains the inscription than the earlier interpretation that it was a misspelled or abbreviated Greek form meaning "belonging to Pilate."

The professor argued the ring likely did not belong to Pilate himself, but may have been worn by a lower-status worker who was carrying out administrative business connected to him.

ANCIENT CHRISTIAN AMULET UNEARTHED AFTER 1,500 YEARS MAY HOLD BIBLICAL SECRET

"Understanding the ring gives us more insight into what the Roman administration of early Roman Judea looked like, in terms of how authority was distributed into the lower echelons of the political structure," Bonesho told UCLA officials in a press release.

"Looking at the poor quality of the ring, the Greek transliteration, the fact that those who used seal rings, like secretaries, are more likely to have been enslaved or formerly enslaved workers — all of that gives us insight into what was happening then," she added.

Fox News Digital reached out to Bonesho for further comment.

The research is "really interesting," Candida Moss, a historian of early Christianity, told Fox News Digital.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Moss, the Edward Cadbury Professor of Theology at the University of Birmingham, said the new interpretation could help resolve a years-old puzzle: If the inscription refers to Pilate, why is the ring so cheaply made?

"This isn't an expensive ring, the kind of thing that you would expect the person who is the governor of the whole area to have," Moss said.

Moss concurred that the ring may have been used by someone working under Pilate and acting with his authority.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"When they made business decisions or legal decisions, they used his ring to kind of set a seal and show that they had the authority [of Pontius Pilate] and, by extension, of the whole Roman bureaucracy behind them," Moss said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Beyond its archaeological significance, Moss said the ring may offer new insight into the biblical account of Jesus' crucifixion, particularly a detail in the Gospel of John.

John's account says Pilate wrote the inscription identifying Jesus as "King of the Jews."

Moss said the ring may illustrate how an act carried out by a subordinate under Pilate's authority could nevertheless be attributed to Pilate himself.

"I think the ring helps us understand why the Bible says that Pilate wrote the inscription that was put on the cross of Jesus, even though we know as historians that he couldn't possibly have written it himself," Moss said.

"He delegated that work to someone else," she said.

item.title: Trump gives Smithsonian days to replace 'strange modernist sculpture' with Founding Father
item.description: President Donald Trump demands a 30-foot George Washington statue replace the "Infinity" sculpture outside the National Museum of American History in Washington.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump is calling on the Smithsonian to replace a decades-old modernist sculpture outside the National Museum of American History with a towering, 30-foot statue of George Washington.

In social media posts late Friday, Trump said the "Infinity" sculpture that has stood outside the museum since 1967 "says nothing about America," while Washington, he argued, "more than anyone else, says everything about America."

Trump also called for the museum to open a five-year exhibition honoring Washington that would run through Feb. 22, 2032, the 300th anniversary of the first president’s birth.

INSIDE THE BEHEMOTH SMITHSONIAN MUSEUM NETWORK DRAWING FIRE FROM THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION

Trump also wants the Smithsonian to install an 11-foot statue of Washington in the museum’s Flag Hall by Constitution Day on Sept. 17. The statue was featured at the recent Freedom 250 Grand Prix race.

"Immediately design and display a five-year exhibition worthy of the Life, Sacrifice, and Contributions of George Washington," Trump wrote.

"Then, as soon as it is ready, install a 30-foot Washington Colossus where ‘Infinity’ stands today," he added.

"Infinity," created by New York artist José de Rivera, was commissioned by the federal government and installed outside the museum in 1967.

It is unclear whether Trump can order the Smithsonian to make the changes. The institution is outside the executive branch and is overseen by a Board of Regents that includes Vice President JD Vance, Chief Justice John Roberts, lawmakers from both parties and citizen members.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Smithsonian for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Trump has repeatedly criticized how the Smithsonian presents American history, particularly as the country celebrates its 250th anniversary.

EXCAVATION SET TO BEGIN ON TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S 250-FOOT TRIUMPHAL ARCH AMID LEGAL BATTLE

In his posts Friday, he accused the National Museum of American History of giving too little attention to Washington and other Founding Fathers.

Trump singled out Washington’s crossing of the Delaware River on Christmas night in 1776 and the American victory at Trenton, saying the museum does not give those events the attention they deserve.

"He is easily America’s Greatest Hero," Trump wrote of Washington. "Without him, our Country and our Freedoms wouldn’t exist."

Trump also criticized the Smithsonian’s recently ended Center for Restorative History, an initiative created to spotlight stories that have been excluded from the national historical narrative.

Trump said the museum should instead create a "Center for American Heroes."

"Tell the stories of Americans who faced great challenges, overcame them, built great things, defended our Country, made America better, and helped our Nation more fully live up to our Founding Ideals," he wrote.

SUPREME COURT CHIEF JUSTICE PRAISES OUTGOING SMITHSONIAN LEADER WHO WAS UNDER PRESSURE FROM TRUMP ADMIN

Those criticisms have also led to action by the White House.

In March 2025, Trump signed an executive order aimed at eliminating what the White House called "divisive narratives" and "improper ideology" at the Smithsonian.

The White House followed this year with a report criticizing the Smithsonian, including what it said was a lack of attention to Washington and other Founding Fathers.

In July, Trump ordered his administration to place signs outside the National Museum of American History telling visitors that some exhibits are inaccurate.

In a statement last year, the Smithsonian’s Board of Regents said it was committed to keeping the institution nonpartisan and its scholarship free from political or partisan influence.

The board also acknowledged that the Smithsonian "can and must do more" and directed its leadership to ensure museum content is unbiased.

Smithsonian secretary Lonnie Bunch announced last week that he will step down at the end of the year.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: 'RedZone' returns for 18th season and, despite 15-second commercials, could still be on in the White House
item.description: Scott Hanson confirms 'RedZone' will air limited 15-second commercials between plays this season, but promises fewer ads than last year's count
item.content:encoded:
The NFL's popular "RedZone" broadcast returns for its 18th season on Sunday, and while the focus is seemingly on how many commercials the previously commercial-free program will air, host Scott Hanson has other things up his sleeve.

But first, the commercials thing:

"There will be, there will be what people define as commercials," Hanson told OutKick recently. "The plan is right now to have a limited number of 15-second commercials only in between plays.

'NFL REDZONE' HOST SCOTT HANSON SAYS HE UNDERSTANDS FAN FRUSTRATION OVER COSTLY STREAMING SUBSCRIPTIONS

"So we're on a Dallas Cowboys drive. OK, first-and-10 after a 5-yard gain. They're walking back to the huddle. That's when we will splice in one standalone, 15-second commercial. I can confirm that for you."

"RedZone" aired 16 advertisements of some kind at one point last season, which marked a significant increase for what was once seven hours of commercial-free programming.

Hanson said fears that the number will increase to start the 2026 season are unfounded. In fact, there will be fewer at the start of the season. That, of course, says nothing about what will happen later this season, but Hanson isn’t making those decisions.

"The rest of it is up to the business folks and Uncle Scott doesn't make the decisions when it comes to the business folks at the NFL," he said. "But yes, there will be advertisements, a limited number, what I would describe as a limited amount, but fans can make their own minds up about that."

Fans made up their minds about "RedZone" and Hanson a long time ago, and those fans have come from some unlikely places.

"I've been told we've been on in the White House in the last two administrations, so both sides of the aisle," Hanson said.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

"I've been told by the players ... Tom Brady, loves ‘RedZone,’ loved it when he was a player, when he was playing on Monday Night Football or Thursday night football or the bye week, he was watching ‘RedZone.’

"Josh Allen — one of the faces of the NFL today — loves ‘RedZone.’ When he's playing on an off day or whatever, if he can watch ‘RedZone.’ So it's just, it's, it's a phenomenon."

Hanson, back with Lowe's for the second year of the popular "Earn Your Sunday" campaign along with Dak Prescott, Christian McCaffrey and Justin Jefferson, is something of a renaissance man.

He's visited six of the planet's seven continents and promises to eventually make it to Antarctica, the only continent he's missed.

Hanson has cage dived with great white sharks and found himself at somewhat safe distances from lions on the Serengeti. He's also visited the Great Wall of China.

All that begs some rapid fire questions:

So, what's his adventure vacation preference, running with the bulls in Pamplona or climbing Mount Kilimanjaro?

"I've done both," Hanson said. "Kilimanjaro was more beautiful. Running with the bulls required more courage. Running with the bulls."

More afraid of great white sharks or lions?

"Lions, because you don't have bars in front of you when you go on safari in the Serengeti plain," Hanson said. "I had bars in front of me when the great whites came up."

Because he visited both China and Mexico, we have to ask: Mexican or Chinese food?

"Oh, Mexican," Hanson said. "Only because in China, the Chinese food is not like American Chinese food. Let me just tell you that I ate a thing called duck dong. And I'm like, what is duck dong? I like it, it's real tasty, until they slowed down, and I learned they were speaking English, and they were saying duck tongue.

"Duck tongue is what they were feeding me. Yeah, no. Give me Mexican."

Seven hours of RedZone begins at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

item.title: Former Bond girl says next 007 should be 'another gorgeous man' as James Bond decision
item.description: Alison Papworth weighed in on who should play James Bond in the iconic film franchise. The actress appeared in "For Your Eyes Only" and "Octopussy."
item.content:encoded:
The search for the next 007 is underway, and former Bond girl Alison Papworth has a clear message: leave one thing untouched.

"What do I hope? I know they’re about to announce the next Bond, aren’t they?" the actress, who also works as a director for a London-based design and consultancy firm, told Fox News Digital. "And we’re all waiting with bated breath."

"If they’re true to the books, I hope it’s a man," she said. "A man, just a man. Yes, I think it would be very strange if it were a woman. Don’t you? It would be a totally different thing. So I hope it’s another man, another gorgeous man."

AMAZON ANNOUNCES SEARCH FOR NEXT JAMES BOND IS UNDERWAY, AS HOLLYWOOD CASTING CHOICES COME UNDER SCRUTINY

Papworth’s comments came before Gary Oldman said on "The Morning Show" that his "Slow Horses" costar Jack Lowden could be the next James Bond.

"Jack, it’s been rumored that he’s on the shortlist," Oldman said on the Canadian talk show. "We’re going to find out pretty soon, aren’t we? Because they have picked him. They have made their choice, but they have not announced it yet. So my fingers are crossed for Jack."

According to Deadline, Oldman later clarified his comments, saying: "There’s six people on a shortlist. I heard a rumor that they’ve picked James Bond, but they haven’t announced it yet, which is their prerogative. So I do not know [who has got the part], but I’m hoping it’s Jack."

Amazon MGM Studios gained creative control of the James Bond franchise in 2025 after forming a joint venture with longtime Bond producers Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli.

WATCH: BOND GIRL ALISON PAPWORTH REVEALS HER HOPE FOR THE NEXT 007

In May, the studio announced that the search for the next James Bond was underway. Denis Villeneuve is set to direct the next installment, with Steven Knight writing the screenplay. Daniel Craig last played 007 in 2021's "No Time to Die."

People magazine reported that Paul Mescal, Jacob Elordi and Jack O'Connell are among the actors rumored to be in the running to take over the iconic role.

The upcoming release will be the 26th Bond film in the more than 60-year-old franchise.

Papworth appeared in 1981’s "For Your Eyes Only" and 1983’s "Octopussy," both of which starred Roger Moore.

"He was an absolute gentleman," she said. "Yes, I know everybody says it. I only have fabulous, fabulous memories of him being funny, telling the best jokes. Very dry, very droll."

"One thing I really remember about him, when we were in India, there was a stuntman, I think it was a stuntman. He used to smuggle beef drippings in his luggage for Roger because he loved it. It was very funny, and it stuck in my mind all those years later."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Being a Bond girl had its benefits. Papworth recalled being flown first class to Rio de Janeiro, where vodka was flowing for the cast, and she tried caviar for the first time. In between filming, she would observe Moore playing Backgammon at picture-worthy destinations.

But life on set wasn't always as luxurious.

"It was the middle of winter doing the scenes for 'Octopussy' where we were fighting in the castle," Papworth recalled. "We learned to stunt fight, and it was supposed to be in India. But we were at Pinewood Studios, and it was below freezing. All the girls had these red bodysuits on with big capes. We were so cold, we had thermals on underneath, so we probably looked about five pounds heavier."

Papworth didn’t expect to appear in two Bond films. She recalled a publicity director once telling her, "Once you’ve done a Bond movie, you get thrown on the Bond Girl scrap heap." But Broccoli, daughter of longtime Bond producer Albert "Cubby" Broccoli, had a different idea.

"You can imagine my surprise when I got the call from Barbara Broccoli saying, 'You’re on the next one, Alison,'" she said. "And it stayed with me. Bond has stayed with me. It’s changed my life. My two best friends, I met one on 'For Your Eyes Only,' Vanya Seager; she was another Bond girl. And I met my other best friend, Carole Ashby, on 'Octopussy.' Carol was there when my baby was born. Vanya and I, we speak every day. I speak to them both every day."

"So without Bond, I wouldn’t have those two incredible bonds," she added.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

After appearing in two Bond movies, Papworth continued acting and modeling. By the time she reached her 30s, however, her modeling career was "leveling out."

"My husband had lots of properties, and I’d always loved interior design," she said. "I’m totally self-taught, but I’m passionate about it. And he just started giving me properties to do, and that developed into our business, which has been running successfully for all these years. I still love it. And after he died, I carried on. He taught me well."

Today, Papworth is a director at Camhall Design & Consultancy, an interior design company based in the U.K. It has completed projects in London, New York, Boston and the Bahamas. She also helped launch Lustre & Lustre London, which offers "luxury cleaning services."

Papworth and her close pal, Joan Collins, also teamed up to raise funds for Shooting Star Children's Hospices. According to the organization's site, it supports, "babies, children and young people with life-limiting conditions, and their families, across south-west London, north-west London and Surrey."

Papworth still has fond memories of her time bringing the Bond stories to life.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"I love show business," she said. "I really do. It’s fabulous. And maybe I’m lucky that I’m not super famous, so I can have a private life. I’m not like my dear friend Joan who gets stopped everywhere. I’m lucky because I can dip in and out of it."

"I still do signings," Papworth continued. "It went quiet through my 30s and 40s. And then, I don’t know. Bond fans are very good at tracking you down. I started to get invites to do signings. I remember doing my first signing in Birmingham at this huge exhibition center. My husband and my kids came because I was a first-time signer. There were all 'Star Wars,' 'Doctor Who,' astronauts, boxers, and little me."

item.title: White Sox amateur scouting director Mike Shirley resigns on heels of verbal harassment allegations
item.description: Mike Shirley allegedly made racial and sexist comments at the Area Code Games, leading to his resignation as Chicago White Sox scouting director.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago White Sox amateur scouting director Mike Shirley has resigned, with the organization announcing the news on Saturday prior to the team's 6-5 win against the St. Louis Cardinals.

Shirley, who was in his seventh season in the leadership role, was alleged to have made inappropriate racial and sexist comments about coworkers and in front of coworkers, according to The Athletic.

The report said that Shirley was placed on administrative leave after an anonymous tip was made to the White Sox regarding his conduct at the Area Code Games in Long Beach, Calif., in August. The Area Code Games is a scouting event that welcomes high school players and is attended by scouting directors, other scouting personnel, as well as front-office employees.

LOS ANGELES ANGELS FIRED ADVANCE SCOUT NICKNAMED 'BASEBALL SPY' AFTER HE WAS CAUGHT FILMING ROCKIES

Chicago's latest investigation into Shirley also included allegations of vulgar language about females and their bodies, sources told The Athletic.

It is the White Sox's policy not to comment on personnel decisions, according to MLB.com.

Shirley had been the subject of at least one other internal investigation in the past in which an anonymous tip was reportedly received from a former White Sox employee who claimed to have left their role regarding Shirley's behavior toward scouts "from underrepresented groups," The Athletic reported.

Shirley did not receive any disciplinary action after the investigation reportedly found no wrongdoing.

The 56-year-old was named the director of amateur scouting for the White Sox in September 2019 after serving as an assistant scouting director and a cross-checker from 2010-2018.

Shirley and his department's work this year was highly focused on Chicago holding the top pick in the MLB Draft for just the third time in franchise history.

The White Sox, who also held a record Draft pool of $20,489,500, selected shortstop Roch Cholowsky out of UCLA at first overall. Chicago shut down Cholowsky for the remainder of the season in August, citing right wrist soreness.

item.title: ‘Family Affair’ star Kathy Garver says failed remake ‘sucked,’ reveals what went wrong
item.description: Kathy Garver called the 2002 "Family Affair" remake terrible, saying Gary Cole and Tim Curry couldn't replicate the original cast's deep warmth.
item.content:encoded:
Kathy Garver is not holding back about the failed 2002 remake of "Family Affair."

In a new interview with Fox News Digital, Garver — who is gearing up to celebrate the 60th anniversary of "Family Affair" by hosting a special marathon featured on Catchy Comedy — explained why the reboot lacked the chemistry, warmth and familial bond that made the classic show so beloved.

"Excuse my language, but it sucked," Garver, who portrayed Cissy in the original series, said. "And it did for many reasons."

'FAMILY AFFAIR' STAR TALKS 'SURVIVING CISSY,' SEEING ANISSA JONES FOR THE LAST TIME AND ALLEGED SITCOM CURSE

The original "Family Affair" premiered in 1966 and followed bachelor Bill Davis as he unexpectedly became the guardian of his late brother and sister-in-law's three children: Cissy, Buffy and Jody. 

Brian Keith played Bill, while Sebastian Cabot portrayed the family’s butler, Mr. French.

The 2002 remake featured Gary Cole as Bill Davis and Tim Curry as Mr. French. Although Garver praised both actors, she said they brought entirely different qualities to the characters audiences had already grown attached to.

KELSEY GRAMMER ADMITS IT'S 'EXHAUSTING' WHEN MOVIES TRY TO ALTER HISTORY TO FIT MODERN TASTES

"I think it’s very difficult to do a remake," Garver said. "When they see Gary Cole, they say, ‘Well, that’s not Uncle Bill.’"

Cole was "great in ‘NCIS,’" Garver said, but "as you know, he’s no Brian Keith."

Keith’s appeal, she explained, came from the contrast between his tough exterior and his tenderness toward the children.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Brian Keith was "this macho guy, the ex-Marine," Garver said. "And here he is, this loving dad."

TIM CURRY'S CAUSE OF DEATH REVEALED

Garver also felt Curry’s portrayal of Mr. French was too far removed from Cabot’s understated performance.

"Tim Curry had a whole different take on it," she said. "It was very good, but it wasn’t in a situation-comedy vein. It was like the Tim Curry show.

"And, so, that didn’t quite mesh with Sebastian Cabot, who was a wonderful actor."

Garver described Curry’s Mr. French as "loud and boisterous," while Cabot’s version was "much more low-key."

ORIGINAL 'LITTLE HOUSE' VILLAIN RETURNS FOR REBOOT WITH WARNING FOR NEW NELLIE

Cabot’s performance was also rooted in his character’s love for the children, Garver said, something she felt the remake failed to convey.

"He, too, did everything in love," she said. "And, basically, he loved the children. And I think that was missing from Tim Curry."

WATCH: ‘FAMILY AFFAIR’ STAR KATHY GARVER SAYS FAILED REMAKE ‘SUCKED,’ REVEALS WHAT WENT WRONG

The actress said the original cast members brought an authentic sense of family to the show because their characters genuinely cared for one another.

"Each individual person on the original ‘Family Affair’ had a family that they loved," Garver said.

‘BRADY BUNCH’ CAST MADE NEARLY NOTHING FROM DECADES OF RERUNS, EVE PLUMB CLAIMS

Garver credited that emotional connection with helping the show stand out from other sitcoms of its era.

"I think it was a groundbreaker," she said. "It was the first of its kind — a single father, or a single uncle, single relative, that all of a sudden gets three orphan children."

The series also benefited from its production quality, according to Garver. She noted that "Family Affair" was among the early television sitcoms filmed in color and that many of the cast and crew members came from the movie industry.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"So, it was a real quality kind of show," she said.

Garver said the original series also featured "relatable characters" and storylines that continue to resonate with audiences.

"It has stories that endure today," she said. "And, so, it remains relatable, I believe, because it’s a family. And how — what do I do with the family? How do I deal with these problems? And it shows you that."

She also believed the warmth of the original series was reflected in the way the characters interacted with one another.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"People really like each other — what a concept," Garver said. "People aren’t yelling and screaming at them. You have this very calm person that’s listening to you."

Garver said the original cast’s chemistry was also visible in their performances.

"Our creator, Ed Hartman, who was just a fabulous writer, creator and producer, told me, ‘Kathy, it’s in the eyes. You act through your eyes. What is coming through them?’

"I think that warmth is something that’s sustained."

For Garver, the enduring appeal of "Family Affair" comes down to the emotional comfort it continues to provide viewers.

She described the show as "a comfort" and compared watching it to "taking a bite of the comfort cake."

"It’s not all this chaos, but something that’s beautiful and lovely and watchable," Garver said.

Catchy Comedy Network will celebrate the sitcom’s 60th anniversary with a special programming event Sunday, Sept. 13. Garver will host the marathon and share memories of portraying Cissy throughout all five seasons.

The event will feature eight of Garver’s favorite episodes, showcasing memorable storylines and Cissy’s journey from adolescence to young adulthood.

item.title: ‘Food divorce’ trend among couples could drive them apart, experts warn
item.description: The "food divorce" trend has some couples eating separately, but experts warn the growing trend erodes relationship quality and emotional well-being over time.
item.content:encoded:
Between differing diet plans, food intolerances and conflicting work schedules, some couples are choosing "food divorce," a term circulating on social media for partners who intentionally cook, order and eat their meals separately.

While taking separate paths at mealtime might solve logistical headaches, experts warn that splitting up at the dinner table can come at a cost to the relationship.

Shared family meals can help people reconnect, build stronger emotional bonds and reduce stress, according to health institutions like Mayo Clinic. 

‘QUIET QUITTING’ IN MARRIAGE: THE SUBTLE SIGNS A SPOUSE HAS EMOTIONALLY CHECKED OUT

For couples, experts say regularly eating apart could become a concern if it reflects broader emotional distance or reduces opportunities to spend meaningful time together.

Nutrition experts emphasize the issue is often less about the food itself and more about the lost opportunity for a built-in daily checkpoint.

"I think it reflects many people's very busy schedules," Tanya Freirich, a North Carolina-based registered dietitian nutritionist, told Fox News Digital.

"Mealtime can be a time to unite, to communicate, to build social relationships and foster a connection," she said. "If we're eating completely alone or at different times than important people in our lives, it may foster a little bit of disconnection."

DOCTORS SAY 8 FORGOTTEN HABITS COULD HELP FIGHT STRESS, OBESITY AND CHRONIC DISEASE

Eating separately can contribute to a "roommate dynamic," experts note. Without regular time to reconnect and discuss the day, couples may have fewer opportunities for communication.

The practice can also contribute to isolation, according to Freirich.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"Communities all around the world for thousands of years have come together around mealtimes," she said. 

"If so many Americans are eating every meal alone for many days or most of their days, that certainly can't be great for mental health or well-being."

There can also be practical drawbacks because preparing separate meals or ordering from different restaurants may increase grocery costs, preparation time and kitchen cleanup.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Additionally, eating solo can affect individual dietary habits. Studies show people dining alone are more likely to eat quickly, mindlessly scroll on their phones or settle for heavily processed convenience foods compared to when they share meals with others.

Couples can accommodate different dietary needs without preparing entirely separate meals. 

For those navigating specific calorie targets, plant-based diets or medical restrictions, Freirich recommended building "modular" or "choose your own adventure" meals as a more efficient method.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"Something like a deconstructed taco night, grain bowls, a pasta or noodle night or even a sheet pan meal where you're creating each food on its own," the expert said. 

"So the protein, the carb, the veggies are being cooked separately. And then you get to decide your portions and make your own meal from those ingredients that can meet everyone's needs."

When conflicting schedules or caregiving duties make daily dinners impossible, experts recommend prioritizing quality over frequency. 

Even sharing a quick weekend breakfast or setting aside one designated night a week can help maintain connection.

"Be very intentional to connect when you can," Freirich suggested.

"Make that a really special meal. Be intentional with your connection. Put the phone away, and actually enjoy the other person's company."

item.title: Hollywood producer spent 25 years praying for Tinseltown, says 'you can't hate them'
item.description: Hollywood Prayer Network founder Karen Covell celebrates 25 years of supporting entertainment industry storytellers through prayer, community and faith-based mentorship.
item.content:encoded:
Hollywood is a place many Christians have condemned; Karen Covell has spent 25 years asking them to pray for the people who work there instead. She is the founder of the Hollywood Prayer Network and sees the town as her greatest ministry.

After all, screenwriters have long preached the maxim "story is everything," and if stories create meaning and influence emotions and shape identity, then Hollywood is the most influential mission field there ever was.

That’s what Covell was thinking when she began the faith-based organization that, along with her staff and now 170-plus chapters in 42 countries, just celebrated its 25th anniversary with a Gatsby-themed gala in downtown Los Angeles.

FORMER DISNEY STAR DAVID HENRIE REJECTED 'SECULAR' HOLLYWOOD LIFESTYLE AFTER LIFE-CHANGING MONASTERY VISIT

Founded in 2001, the Hollywood Prayer Network, through prayer, community and resources, supports the entertainment industry’s storytellers and believes the next generation of actors, writers, directors and producers doesn't have to maneuver Tinseltown alone.

The organization offers everything from intercessory prayer and professional discipleship programs to networking and Bible studies.

"We have a beautiful community here. You couldn't get me out of this place for anything because the people that are here are wonderful," Covell told Fox News Digital.

It was more than 25 years ago when Covell, along with her composer husband, Jim Covell, saw and felt the need for believers in Hollywood to have support.

KEVIN SORBO BLASTS HOLLYWOOD 'BLACKLISTING' OF CONSERVATIVES AS 'SEVENTH GRADE MEAN GIRLS' CULTURE

"It's competitive, a lot of people look for work, we're all freelancers and we wanted to support the people of faith here who really felt like they had one foot in the church and one foot in the Hollywood entertainment industry and neither one liked each other," Covell, who originally came to Los Angeles to attend the University of Southern California, explained.

While the two had already started a prayer group, they found that those coming to Los Angeles out of the church arrived in the city, as she put it, already "beat up."

SKILLET’S JOHN COOPER SAYS CHRISTIANS WHO CALL ROCK MUSIC ‘DEMONIC’ ARE ‘GETTING THE GOSPEL WRONG’

"I knew Hollywood didn't like the church because we were really terrible to them — we boycotted, we threw out our TVs, we burned their books — we wouldn't go to their movies, you know, but I believed if you pray for somebody, you can't hate them," Covell said.

She recalled hearing stories from people in the group whose families, pastors and friends had warned them not to go to Los Angeles — that it was Satan's pit and that they couldn't live there.

HOLLYWOOD PRODUCER BEHIND 'APOLLO 13' REJECTS POLITICS IN HIS MOVIES, SEEKS TO UNITE AUDIENCES

"And I said, ‘This is ridiculous. We should be storytellers. We should be creative. God created us to be creative.’"

So, Covell decided to try to figure out a way to build a bridge between the church in America and Hollywood.

NEARLY 500 PUBLIC FIGURES FROM POLITICS TO HOLLYWOOD WILL READ BIBLE COVER TO COVER TO MARK AMERICA'S 250TH

"I thought, ‘I've got to get the church to start understanding the beauty and the importance of Hollywood,’" she said.

Since then, whether someone is a believer or not, the HPN has prayed for people ranging from fledgling singers to the likes of Britney Spears during her periods of intense tabloid scrutiny and personal struggle. Paris Hilton has received intercessory prayer while Robert Downey Jr. was lifted up during his public battle with addiction. 

There have been many prayers for wildlife, crisis relief efforts and, recently, for celebrity blogger Perez Hilton after his distressing livestream and subsequent hospitalization.

NEW STUDY REVEALS THE SINGLE MOST CRITICAL FACTOR IN WHETHER CHILDREN KEEP THEIR FAITH INTO ADULTHOOD

Through its monthly Kids Prayer Calendar, "Ones2Watch," members support child and teen actors in prayer before they face major industry pressures.

The organization has established numerous community groups geared toward directors, dancers, writers, comedians and people working in technology and AI. 

It has local chapters across the United States, each serving entertainment professionals through mentorship, networking and worship. It also has its own app, which lists its resources, local chapters around the world and community events.

"We have gatherings of people all over the city and all over the country and the world who say, 'Yes, it's important to be storytellers,'" Covell said, noting she has found what attacks artists is isolation, discouragement and fear. "Those three things can all be combated in community."

For her part, Covell credits her 42-year marriage to a husband who counts the days they’ve been together as a big part of her own success. The two, who recently finished a book titled "Confessions of a Hollywood Marriage," as she put it, "pray together every day and walk with each other through the hard and good times."

"It's not a how-to book. It's not anything to help people. It is just us telling the story of our marriage and how it's been such a beautiful and amazing journey for the last 42 years," Covell said. "It's not because we're any different or special. … We know people see so many bad marriages that they lose hope that it's possible. And we just let people know, this is the greatest gift."

Just last year, Covell chose to step down from producing and instead devote herself fully to the Hollywood Prayer Network, which she said has been growing quickly of late.

It wasn’t that way at the start.

"I take credit for having, I think, the slowest-growing ministry on the planet. It was just one person at a time. Would you pray for Hollywood?" Covell quipped. "And I just kept going."

Recently, staff and members posted a video on the organization’s social media showing Covell jokingly preparing for a "Netflix documentary" about what it’s like to be a Christian in Hollywood. The viral posts included disclaimers clarifying that the Netflix part was just a ruse based on a popular online video trend.

Covell just wants to keep supporting storytellers as they tell great stories and reminding them that they’re not alone in the process.

"As a producer, I worked in Hollywood and in the secular industry. My husband is still writing music in the secular industry. We love the commercial industry of Hollywood. We love the people, we love the projects, we love the place," she said. 

"This ministry started growing, and I slowly started seeing other people come with the same feeling of, ‘Well, let's build community. Let's be together. Let's love the people we're here with. Let's celebrate being storytellers.’

"We want to tell great stories that inspire people, that encourage people. And we want to know that we're not alone doing it. So, that's my purpose with the prayer network."

item.title: Dan Dakich says women might be the reason for Nike's downfall: 'They p----d them off'
item.description: Dan Dakich says Nike's collapse stems from alienating women buyers and losing ground to Athleta and Lululemon in a booming competitive market.
item.content:encoded:
It's no secret at this point that Nike is taking a nosedive.

They're being mercilessly mocked online for releasing a low-effort series of NBA jerseys, and their stock has plummeted so much that they are set to get the boot from the S&P 100 later this month.

While plenty of personalities have weighed in, OutKick's Dan Dakich decided to throw his hat in the ring and discuss just how bad things have gotten for the failing athletic apparel giant.

OUTKICK'S CRAIG CARTON REVEALS THE REAL REASON NIKE STOCK IS IN THE TANK: 'THEY'RE FAILING MISERABLY'

On a recent episode of his "Don't @ Me" show, Dakich was joined by Dan Zaksheske and Jason Hammer to break down the missteps committed by Nike that led them to this lowly state.

Zaksheske opined that the "go woke, go broke" mantra certainly applies here, but we have to take everything into account, including complacency.

"I would compare Nike to Disney," Zaksheske stated. "They're just resting on their laurels. They're not creating anything new."

Hammer offered a different perspective, giving credit to FOX Business's Taylor Riggs for the insight.

TED CRUZ TAKES VICTORY LAP AS ICONIC AMERICAN BRAND'S STOCK PLUNGES TO 12-YEAR LOW

"They gave a middle finger to the retailers," he said. "They thought they could go directly to the consumer and that didn't work, coming out of a COVID-era where people were desperate to actually go out and go to the stores, see the displays, and the Nike displays weren't there anymore."

Dakich certainly agreed with his guests, but he offered his own take on the matter.

"Local competition," he said when pointing a finger at Nike's problems. "Athleta is booming. Lululemon is booming. It used to be Nike or Adidas, which one are you going to buy?"

Competition in the marketplace can either force you to improve or make you watch from the sidelines, and Nike seems to be doing the latter.

Alienating the local retailers was a big mistake from Nike, but Dakich posits that the company has a female problem, too.

"Women have said, 'Bulls---, don't insult us,'" Dakich said. "Who's buying stuff? It ain't me and it ain't you (Hammer)... it is freaking women, and (Nike) p----d them off."

There's no doubt that Nike is facing a litany of issues, and Dakich, Zaksheske and Hammer only scratched the surface of what appears to be a catastrophic crossroads for the former kings of athletic wear.

If they want to climb back to the top of the mountain, they will definitely have to look in the mirror and do some soul-searching.

Only time will tell if that happens before it's too late.
